title: Race Splits — a pace planner for 5K to marathon
description: Enter a recent race, from a mile to a marathon or a custom distance, and Riegel's formula T2 = T1 × (D2/D1)^1.06 predicts a new distance. The exponent can be changed. The prediction becomes a goal you can edit, and the page turns it into an even, negative or positive split plan with a split for every mile or kilometre, a pace chart, a cumulative table, and an optional altitude tip that uses the same rule of thumb as the Lab's Thin Air page.
prompt: Build a race pace planner for 5K to marathon. Predict race times from a recent race with Riegel's formula T2 = T1 × (D2/D1)^1.06, and let me edit the exponent. Build a split plan (even, negative split or positive), with per-mile or per-km splits in a chart and a table, cumulative time, and an optional altitude adjustment tip that links to the Lab's Thin Air page (../lab/009-thin-air.html). Add a mi/km toggle. The spec should check the Riegel math and that the splits add up to the goal time within 1 second.

methodology: Formula oracle: the spec computes T1 × (D2/D1)^k itself for 5K→half, 10K→marathon and mile→5K, and at exponents 1.00, 1.06 and 1.08. At 1.00 the prediction must reduce to plain pace scaling, and an h:mm:ss input must parse to the right number of seconds.

Sum invariant: the spec adds up the split times shown in the table and requires them to equal the goal to within 1 s. It checks this through the UI for a half marathon in miles and in km and for a marathon, and through the plan hook for 450 combinations of goal, distance, unit and strategy. The page rounds cumulative times and takes differences, so the rounding error can't build up.

Segment structure: a half marathon has 13 full miles plus a 0.11 partial, or 21 km plus 0.10, and a marathon has 26 miles plus 0.22. Each even split must be within 1 s of goal ÷ distance, and the average pace readout must match (1:45:29 half → 5:00/km).

Strategy math: for the linear pace ramp p(x) = avg·(1 + a(1 − 2x/D)), the halves must be goal/2 × (1 ± a/2). With a 4 % negative split, a 4:00 marathon must split 2:02:24 + 1:57:36, each mile's pace must be quicker than the one before, and each split must be within 1 s of the spec's own integral. Positive splits must mirror this.

Edges: malformed times (25:75, words), an exponent outside 1.00–1.20 and a blank goal each give a specific message, and Use prediction clears them. Custom distances keep their physical length when the unit changes (8 mi → 12.87 km). The altitude tip must give 0.1 % × 5.28² ≈ 2.8 % at 5,280 ft, link to the Thin Air page, and add that time to the goal.
risks: Rounding each split separately can make the splits add up to a few seconds more or less than the goal over 26 miles. The page rounds the cumulative times instead, and the spec checks the sum.
The partial final segment (0.11 mi, 0.22 mi, 0.10 km) is easy to leave out or to give a full unit's time.
Riegel's formula is an empirical fit for roughly 3.5 to 230 minutes. It overpredicts for runners who haven't trained for the longer distance, and the page doesn't claim otherwise.
The altitude model is a deliberately rough rule of thumb shared with Thin Air. Its label says so, and the spec checks the arithmetic, not whether it is physiologically right.
qa.playwright: Most assertions read the rendered table: the spec parses each split and elapsed cell and checks the arithmetic in Node, so a display-rounding bug can't hide behind correct internal numbers. The 450-case sum sweep runs inside one page.evaluate against window.__splits.plan, because doing that through the UI would be slow for no benefit. selectOption, fill and check behave the same on desktop Chrome and the Pixel 7 project, so there was no need for touch-specific code. Nothing on the page is timed, so page.clock isn't needed. The chart is only checked through its aria-label, which is a weak spot.
coverage: Riegel predictions at three distance pairs and three exponents; h:mm:ss parsing
Even splits in miles and km: counts, partial segment, per-split and average pace, sum = goal
Negative and positive plans: halves formula, monotonic pace, per-split integral
450-case sum sweep through the plan hook
Validation messages, custom distances across unit changes, altitude tip, Thin Air link and apply

a11y: Every field is a labelled native input or select, and the unit and strategy choices are toggle buttons with aria-pressed. Validation messages are in alert regions, and the prediction and the summary are aria-live. The split table has column headers, and the chart's aria-label gives the plan type, the number of splits, the average pace and the fastest and slowest splits.
